Both Dichotomine E and Nardostachin are known to interact with Phosphodiesterase 6C, indicating that trans-urocanic acid may influence this pathway via its interaction with Microtubule-associated protein 1B. The shared target of these compounds with Phosphodiesterase 6C suggests a possible mechanism where trans-urocanic acid could modulate the activity of this enzyme through its interaction with the upstream protein. The evidence is consistent across two distinct pathways, reinforcing the likelihood of a functional link between trans-urocanic acid and Phosphodiesterase 6C.
